title: Personal Injury Intake and Cases
description: Intakes, case stages, medical records requests and offers for a personal injury practice.

spec.useCase: Nadia Petrov is a case manager at a personal injury firm and uses this to return new intakes in a day, chase medical records requests and see which signed cases are ready for a demand. Operational tracking only; it holds no legal advice.

business.describes: A small plaintiff-side firm handling auto, premises and workplace injury cases.

text.text: Your personal injury practice in one place. Start with Intakes to call today, track each signed Case through its stages, and keep Records requests and Offers moving. Operational tracking only; strategy and privileged notes stay in the case file.
Collect facts and be kind. The attorney decides whether the firm can help.
Thank the caller and let them tell the story first.
Capture the date of the incident, who was involved and who has treated them.
Flag any date-sensitive item for the attorney right away.
Log the intake and set Call by to the next business day.
Attorney decision: send an engagement agreement or a decline letter.
Every signed case moves through the same stages.
Investigation: preservation letters, scene photos, carrier details.
Treatment: check in with the client every two weeks.
Records and bills: requests out to every provider.
Demand: package reviewed by the attorney and sent.
Negotiation: log every offer under Offers.
Press Request records on the case.
Set a follow-up date one week out.
Past the follow-up date, call the provider and mark Chased.
Escalate to the attorney after the third attempt.
Enter bills as soon as records arrive.
Log the amount, carrier and date
Tell the client the same day
Look at Highest offer on the case before each client update.
